rule.description: A class is reported when the methods it declares structurally evidence at least 6 of the 8 statically-marked model-pipeline responsibilities (graph_construction, training_orchestration, prediction_serving, persistence_io, input_dataset_pipeline, stochastic_sampling, rank_evaluation, session_lifecycle). Evidence is read from call-target and attribute-usage markers in the Pylint AST, so responsibilities stay visible across renames and file moves and vanish when a stage is handed back to a cohesive owner.

checks.description: Pylint plugin message C9001: report every class whose own declared methods structurally evidence at least 6 of the 8 model-pipeline responsibilities, counted from disjoint call-target and attribute-usage markers in the class body.
checks.detected_relation: model class -> absorbed pipeline stages; the class owns graph construction, training orchestration, prediction serving and persistence (its legitimate lifecycle remit) plus input/dataset preparation, stochastic sampling, rank evaluation and session lifecycle stages absorbed from support modules, while those support modules forward back up into the class to perform their own work.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A god class for this case is a single class that has become the de facto owner of nearly the entire recommendation pipeline. Concentrating four pipeline stages beyond the model lifecycle in one class destroys the package's layering: support modules stop owning their logic, and every change to input handling, metrics or session management has to be made in (and reviewed against) the model class that also owns fitting, serving and persistence.

matches.evidence: Pylint C9001 at tensorrec/tensorrec.py:25: God class "TensorRec" in tensorrec.tensorrec concentrates 8 of 8 model-pipeline responsibilities [graph_construction(1 methods), input_dataset_pipeline(3 methods), persistence_io(2 methods), prediction_serving(8 methods), rank_evaluation(6 methods), session_lifecycle(1 methods), stochastic_sampling(1 methods), training_orchestration(1 methods)] across 37 declared methods; threshold is 6 distinct responsibilities. The four stages beyond the model lifecycle are carried by entries E02-E18 (session classmethods, dataset/iterator/TFRecord construction and dimension probing, sampling and batched-alpha math, rank metric bodies and fit-and-score orchestration declared as class members); entries E19-E30 record the inverted donor side, where the evaluation module's metric functions are pass-through wrappers into the class and the session-management module forwards to the class at call time.

excluded.reason: Loss-graph strategy class whose methods legitimately construct TF graph nodes; it evidences only the graph_construction stage (1 of 8) and is far below the rule threshold, so it is intentionally outside the reported relation.

Strategy/algorithm modules consumed through factory interfaces; their classes each evidence at most one pipeline stage inside their own remit and are not part of the concentrated-responsibility relation.
